div.div: Type 3 — signing and token-refresh proxies

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1378px; height: 1px; padding-top: 42px; margin-left: 3px;

div.div: Two problems the platform cannot solve on its own: it does not sign requests, and it does not refresh a token that expires in the middle of a five-hour scan. Both are closed by a service that sits in the path and adds what is missing.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1366px; height: 1px; padding-top: 97px; margin-left: 15px;

div.div: A — SIGV4 SIGNING PROXY

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 198px; height: 1px; padding-top: 153px; margin-left: 32px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #00294D;

div.span:
Reads the body, computes the canonical request and
the HMAC-SHA256 digest over it, and adds the three
headers AWS expects before forwarding:
Authorization · x-amz-date · x-amz-content-sha256

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 228px; height: 1px; padding-top: 153px; margin-left: 1122px;

div.span:
service name execute-api.
Rejects anything unsigned.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-end; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 196px; height: 1px; padding-top: 177px; margin-left: 238px;

div.div: This pattern does not reach a Bedrock Agent. It streams the upstream body straight back, which suits execute-api. InvokeAgent answers with a chunked event stream instead of a JSON document, so the platform receives bytes that {RESPONSE} cannot map. That needs the Bedrock bridge, which collapses the stream into one body.

div.span:
Holds one static bearer
token for the proxy, and
nothing that expires

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 456px; height: 1px; padding-top: 387px; margin-left: 455px;

div.span:
Holds a long-lived refresh token. Before forwarding,
it checks the cached access token and exchanges for
a fresh one if it expires within the next two minutes,
then injects it and passes the body through unchanged.

Sees a valid Okta access
token on every request,
hour five included.

div.div: It now holds a long-lived refresh token, and it has to respect Okta's own rate limits on token exchange

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 664px; height: 1px; padding-top: 829px; margin-left: 17px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Signing belongs in pre_process, never in authenticate

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 648px; height: 1px; padding-top: 849px; margin-left: 19px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Where Kubernetes is available, a Custom Target Adapter replaces
both proxies on this page and neither of them has to be hosted.
Put the signature in pre_process, because a SigV4 or HMAC digest
covers the request body and the body does not exist yet when
authenticate() runs. Use authenticate() for the token exchange,
where its TTL caching earns its keep.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 664px; height: 1px; padding-top: 829px; margin-left: 717px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: A proxy holding credentials is a target of its own

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 648px; height: 1px; padding-top: 849px; margin-left: 719px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Either proxy ends up holding the material that reaches the agent:
an AWS access key pair, or a refresh token good for the length of
the engagement. Both are more valuable than the bearer token
standing in front of them.
Keep it off the public internet where you can, give it credentials
scoped to the one agent, and retire it when scanning ends.
